Posting Title 
Graduate Intern – Agentic AI-Driven Computational Synthesis of PGM-free Fuel Cell Catalysts . 
 Location 
CO - Golden . 
 Position Type 
Intern (Fixed Term) . 
 Hours Per Week 
40 . 
 Working at NLR 
NLR is located at the foothills of the Rocky Mountains in Golden, Colorado is the nation's primary laboratory for energy systems research and development. 
 Join the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR), where world-class scientists, engineers, and experts are accelerating energy innovation through breakthrough research and systems integration. From our mission to our collaborative culture, NLR stands out in the research community for its commitment to an affordable and secure energy future. Spanning foundational science to applied systems engineering and analysis, we focus on solving complex challenges to deliver advanced, secure, reliable, and cost-effective energy solutions. Our work helps strengthen U.S. industries, support job creation, and promote national economic growth.
 
 At NLR, you'll find a mission-driven environment supported by state-of-the-art facilities, multidisciplinary research teams, and strong collaborations with industry, academia, and other national laboratories. We offer robust professional development opportunities, and a competitive benefits package designed to support your career and well-being.

 Job Description 
 The Advance Computing Solutions group in the NLR Computational Science Center has an opening for a graduate intern in computational synthesis, with a particular emphasis on development and utilization of an agentic AI framework that automates the exploration of relevant reaction energetics using machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs). The researcher will work with an interdisciplinary team to develop agentic AI that automates the training of MLIPs of desirable accuracy and uses the trained MLIPs to discern the effect of varying different reaction conditions on the final synthesized Fe-N-C fuel cel catalyst.
  
 We are looking for a dynamic, motivated researcher with a strong technical background and an interest in the mission of NLR. The successful candidate will collaborate with NLR staff and researchers to develop agentic AI for the optimization of Fe-N-C catalyst synthesis.
  
 Responsibilities include:
 
• Development of agentic AI framework that automates the training of MLIPs and the exploration of the combinatorial space of reactions relevant to Fe-N-C catalyst synthesis and their energetics 
• Collaboration with NLR researchers to use the developed AI to study the chemistry of graphitization and Fe incorporation into the N-C matrix for different synthetic precursors, e.g. iron salts and zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF) linkers. 
• Development of AI that processes, analyzes, and visualizes results from simulations provide chemical insight and intuition into important chemical reactions. 
• Authoring, presenting and assisting in the preparation of technical papers, reports and conference proceedings on topics related to AI-automated MLIP studies of the synthesis of Fe-N-C fuel cell catalysts. 
 This role will be a hybrid work arrangement primarily at our South Table Mountain campus with some work from home time. 
 . 
 Basic Qualifications 
Minimum of a 3.0 cumulative grade point average.

Undergraduate: Must be enrolled as a full-time student in a bachelor’s degree program from an accredited institution. 
Post Undergraduate: Earned a bachelor’s degree within the past 12 months. Eligible for an internship period of up to one year.

Graduate: Must be enrolled as a full-time student in a master’s degree program from an accredited institution. 
Post Graduate: Earned a master’s degree within the past 12 months. Eligible for an internship period of up to one year.
Graduate + PhD: Completed master’s degree and enrolled as PhD student from an accredited institution. 

Please Note:
• Applicants are responsible for uploading official or unofficial school transcripts, as part of the application process.
• If selected for position, a letter of recommendation will be required as part of the hiring process.
• Must meet educational requirements prior to employment start date. 
 * Must meet educational requirements prior to employment start date. 
 
 Additional Required Qualifications 
 ·        Excellent written and verbal communication skills. 
 ·        Excellent knowledge of AI automation, including skills files and deterministic frameworks such as LangChain 
 ·        Experience with chemistry and materials science, especially with incorporation of ML/AI into the workflow. 
 ·        Experience with creating python environments for AI/ML tasks and workflows 

 Preferred Qualifications 
 AI workflow automation of MLIP calculations for exploration of the chemical space relevant to Fe-N-C catalyst synthesis. 
   
 Experienced running density functional theory (DFT) software packages such as JDFTx or VASP.  
   
 Experience with the MACE-based machine-learned interatomic potentials, especially foundational models 
 .

 The anticipated closing window for application submission is up to 30 days and may be extended as needed.

Job Profile: / Annual Salary Range: $44,500 - $71,200

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance; 403(b) Employee Savings Plan with employer match*; and sick leave (where required by law). Intern assignments extending beyond six months will be subject to this requirement.

Applications are not kept on file for future positions. Please include a cover letter and resume with each position application.

More on the problems we're solving: https://docs.steel.dev/overview/intro-to-steel

 


THE ROLE

We're looking for exceptional software engineering interns to help build the infrastructure and developer tools powering the next generation of AI agents.
You'll work alongside our engineering team on real technical challenges, from scaling browser infrastructure to building developer tools and experimenting with AI agents. We're a small team that moves fast, and you'll have the opportunity to take ownership, ship production code, and see your work used by developers building some of the most exciting applications in AI.

 - Building and shipping features across Steel's APIs, SDKs, and developer tools

 - Improving the performance and reliability of our browser infrastructure

 - Building open-source demos that showcase what's possible with AI agents and browsers

 - Experimenting with AI models, prompts, and agent frameworks to improve browser automation

 - Working with containers, VMs, proxies, and distributed systems to scale browser sessions

 - Debugging tricky engineering problems and shipping fixes that make Steel faster and more reliable

 - Comfortable writing code and learning new languages, frameworks, and tools

 - Curious about how systems work and excited to solve challenging technical problems

 - Able to take ownership, move quickly, and learn independently

 - Able to work in person from our Toronto office

 - Previous software engineering internship experience

 - Experience building full-stack applications, developer tools, or infrastructure projects

 - Contributions to open-source projects or interesting personal projects

 - Experience with cloud infrastructure, Linux, containers, or distributed systems

 - Experience building with LLMs or AI agents
   
    


APPLYING

If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach out to schedule 2 short technical interviews. After, we'll schedule an onsite at our Toronto office, where you'll work on a small project, discuss ideas, and meet the team.
